subject: Confirming hosting priorities & legacy API exit plan
messages:
From: Sara Knox <sara.knox@medisolve.com>
To: Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwood.com>
Cc: Tom Li <tom.li@medisolve.com>
Date: Mon, 29 Jun 2026 15:22:00 -0700
Subject: Post-demo: hosting priorities & migration note

Connor — thanks for the demo earlier today. Quick recap from our side and a few clarifying questions so we can decide hosting mode (Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private). High level: we run a customer-facing chat product (low-latency, high-throughput) and an internal PII-sensitive enrichment pipeline that currently lives on a legacy GPU cluster behind our firewall. We also have some features calling third-party APIs where we prefer the lowest integration lift.

Current posture:
- Public-facing chat (prod): ~120 QPS peak, avg seq length ~180 tokens, 99th pct latency target ~200ms.
- PII enrichment (internal): must remain in our VPC or on-prem; cannot egress PII.
- Experimentation models: currently using another LLM API (OpenAI) for prototyping.

What we need from Redwood to make a hosting decision:
1) Recommended split: is the right approach Hosted API for chat + Dedicated pool for predictable throughput, and Private (VPC or on-prem) for PII, or should we consolidate onto Dedicated with VPC peering?
2) Migration path: how do you handle model transfer / weights, warm cache, and request fingerprinting to make the cutover from the legacy cluster minimal?
3) Security/compliance: we will need KMS/HSM integration and audit logs for the Private deployment; is Redwood private offering audited logs we can ship into our SIEM?
4) PoC ask: we want a 2-week Private PoC against a small dataset, then a scaling run. What does that plan look like operationally and cost-wise?

Next steps from our side: Tom (cc) is procurement. We are targeting a mid-August cutover window but can be flexible if the migration requires longer. Please reply with a short MAP, a list of technical inputs you need from us, and any blockers.

Thanks — Sara
Sara Knox
Head of Product Operations
MediSolve Inc.

Attachments: medisolve-current-sla.pdf (attached)

From: Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwood.com>
To: Sara Knox <sara.knox@medisolve.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 30 Jun 2026 09:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-demo: hosting priorities & migration note

Sara — great to connect. Short answers up front, then a proposed MAP and list of inputs.

Quick recommendation (high level):
- Hosted API: Use for low-friction features and new experiments (fastest onboarding, pay-as-you-go).
- Dedicated capacity: Best fit for your public-facing chat if you want predictable latency/throughput with reserved GPUs and burst capacity for spikes.
- Private (VPC/on-prem): Required for your PII enrichment pipeline; we can do a Private control plane with customer-managed data plane (VPC peering or on-prem bundle).

Proposed mutual action plan (MAP):
1) Technical intake (this week): we collect specs and traces — model families, model weights availability (or public model names), tokenizer, peak QPS, avg/95/99 latency targets, sequence-length distribution, tokenization mismatch notes.
2) Security intake (3 days): KMS key policies, required audit retention, certs for peering, SOC2 artifacts exchange.
3) Private PoC (2 weeks): deploy Private control plane in a sandbox VPC; run your PII pipeline with synthetic data (no customer PII); validate KMS, audit logs, and latency metrics; provide warmup scripts for KV cache.
4) Dedicated scale run (2–4 weeks): reserve dedicated pool for chat; run soak test at peak QPS with replayed traces; tune batching and cache TTLs.
5) Cutover plan & rollback window (1 week): staged rollout with canary traffic and fallback to existing API for 24–48h.

Technical inputs we need from MediSolve: (please send these as files/links)
- Representative traces (JSON logs or pcap) for chat and enrichment workloads.
- Current tokenization library/version and sample tokenized payloads.
- Inventory of legacy GPU cluster: model files (weights), framework (PyTorch/TF), access method (SCP/S3), and any env constraints.
- Peak QPS by route and expected concurrency per connection.
- Procurement timeline and PO/Security contacts (Tom is fine).

Operational notes / risk flags:
- If you must preserve private keys on-prem, Private will require HSM/KMS integration and a slightly longer security review.
- Model weight transfer for very large weights (>200GB) may be faster via shipped disk for on-prem bundles versus network sync.
- Warm cache: we recommend a short replay window + prefix caching pre-warm script; estimate 4–8 hours to reach steady-state for chat depending on session stickiness.

Attachments: I attached a one-page MAP and our Deploy Options doc (redwood-deploy-options.pdf) to help. I'll loop Marissa and Monica to coordinate the PoC engineering and compliance runbook.

Proposed check-in: 7/7 or 7/8 for a 30-min intake to kick off collection. Does that work?

— Connor
Connor O'Brien
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference

Attachments: MediSolve-MAP-v1.pdf; redwood-deploy-options.pdf

From: Sara Knox <sara.knox@medisolve.com>
To: Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwood.com>
Cc: Tom Li <tom.li@medisolve.com>
Date: Wed, 01 Jul 2026 11:40:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-demo: hosting priorities & migration note

Connor — thanks, that MAP looks good. Quick clarifications and numbers we can share now:
- Chat prod: sustained 80–120 QPS, burst to 180 for short windows; 95th pct latency target 140–180ms after optimization.
- Enrichment pipeline: ~10 QPS but strict data locality; lives on-prem today (3x A100s, models are mixed: one proprietary 160B and several open 7B/13B checkpoints).
- Tokenizer: custom fork of tiktoken v0.4. We'll provide tokenized samples.

Procurement note: Tom (cc) — our target is to have commercial terms signed and PO issued by 2026-08-15; procurement will need SOW for the PoC and a simple MSA. I attached our current SLA and a short list of required audit artifacts.

We can do the intake meeting on 7/7 at 10:00 PT. For the Private PoC we will provide a sanitized dataset and an ops contact who can open temporary VPN for the VPC peering. We are wary of shipping very large weights over the wire — can you confirm Redwood supports disk shipment for initial sync?

Thanks — Sara

Attachment: medisolve-current-sla.pdf

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Sara Knox <sara.knox@medisolve.com>
Cc: Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 07 Jul 2026 09:18:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-demo: hosting priorities & migration note

Sara / Tom — forwarding next engineering steps and a brief ops checklist. Happy to run the intake on 7/7 10:00 PT (we reserved 30 minutes).

Ops checklist and PoC plan (ops owner: Monica Patel)
- Access: please create a read-only S3 bucket or provide one-time SCP access to the legacy model artifacts; if weights >200GB we will accept encrypted shipped disk (FedEx) — we will provide a shipping manifest and a checksum workflow.
- Traces: share a 24–72 hour replay window for chat (anonymized) and a 1–2 hour trace for enrichment pipeline. Drive link preferred.
- VPN/Peering: ops will coordinate with your network engineer; we need CIDR ranges, desired egress rules, and a contact to schedule the peering test.
- Security artifacts: KMS key ARN (if AWS), required retention for audit logs, and SIEM ingestion endpoint.

PoC timeline (detailed):
Week 0: intake + security review (3–5 days)
Week 1–2: Private PoC (sandbox VPC, sample workload, KMS + audit verification)
Week 3–4: Dedicated capacity soak and tuning for chat (if you elect Dedicated for chat)

Risk mitigations:
- Fallback: during cutover we will keep the legacy cluster in read-only mode for 48 hours and route 5–10% traffic as a canary.
- Pre-signed tokens: we can integrate prefix tokenization to preserve behavioral parity across tokenizers.

Action items assigned:
- MediSolve: provide traces, tokenized samples, and ops contact for VPN (Tom).
- Redwood (Monica): send PoC SOW draft and a short runbook; share temporary SSH keys for inventory (if allowed).

I'll upload the PoC SOW to the HubSpot deal today and open a DocuSign envelope for the SOW so procurement can review. See link: https://www.docusign.net/transaction/XYZ-POC-2026

See you 7/7 10:00 PT.

— Marissa
Marissa Cole
Director, Solutions & Customer Engineering | Redwood Inference
